title: Coronary artery bypass surgery (CABG)
what: The surgeon takes a blood vessel from your leg, arm, or chest wall and attaches it around a narrowed heart artery. Blood then reaches the heart by a new route.
why: For severe narrowing of several heart arteries, when stents are not suitable or will not help.
duration: surgery usually takes 3 to 6 hours, with 7 to 10 days in hospital, including 1 to 2 days in intensive care
tell_doctor: All your medicines, especially blood thinners and diabetes medicines. Your doctor will say what to stop and when
Kidney or lung disease, or diabetes
If you smoke. It is best to quit as early as possible

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood tests, an ECG, a heart ultrasound, a coronary angiogram, and sometimes ultrasounds of leg and neck vessels. The clinic will give you a list.

prepare.title: Anesthetist
prepare.text: Before surgery, the anesthetist and surgeon will talk with you. Ask all your questions.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually no food from the night before and no drinks for a few hours. The clinic will tell you the exact time.

prepare.title: Home
prepare.text: Arrange in advance who will help you at home for the first weeks.

bring: Documents and a list of your medicines
Comfortable clothes that open at the front
Things for a 1 to 2 week hospital stay
steps: You change, and IV lines are placed
The anesthetist gives anesthesia, and you fall asleep
The surgeon opens the breastbone. Sometimes the heart is connected to a heart-lung machine
Vessels for the grafts are taken from the leg, arm, or chest wall
The grafts are attached around the narrowed arteries
The breastbone is closed with wires, and the wound is stitched
You wake up in intensive care, sometimes with a breathing tube
feel: Chest pain from the cut. You will get painkillers
Coughing and deep breathing may be hard. You will be taught exercises
after: You start getting up in the first days
For a few weeks, no heavy lifting or pushing up with your arms. This protects the breastbone
Recovery usually takes 2 to 3 months, often with cardiac rehab
Take your medicines exactly as your doctor prescribed
red_flags: Chest pain like before surgery: call emergency services
Severe shortness of breath: call emergency services
A fever over 38°C (100.4°F), or redness or discharge from the wound
Clicking or movement in the breastbone

faq.q: How long do bypass grafts last?
faq.a: Usually many years. They last longer if you do not smoke and keep blood pressure and cholesterol under control.

faq.q: When can I get back to normal life?
faq.a: Light tasks after a few weeks, work and driving usually after 1 to 3 months. Your doctor will give you the timing.

reminders.text: Heart surgery tomorrow. Pack your documents, things, and medicine list. Eat and drink only until the time the clinic gave you.
